calibration.status: tuned on the tuning query set only; provisional for any other data
calibration.keyword_settings: words and two-word phrases, no stemming
calibration.method: Read the keyword cosine, semantic cosine and coverage of the expected ticket and of the strongest other ticket for every tuning query, then chose cut points between the two groups.
observations: Near-verbatim matches: semantic cosine 0.79 to 0.93 and coverage 0.33 to 0.61.
Queries with no useful past ticket (misleading, different product, unfamiliar): coverage 0.29 or lower, with one exception.
The exception is a negation query (semantic 0.82, coverage 0.35). Neither retriever can tell a negated symptom from the symptom itself, so it stays a false match.

Reworded matches: the expected ticket is ranked first by semantic search in 5 of 6 cases, but with semantic cosine 0.35 to 0.63 and coverage under 0.1. That overlaps the scores of unrelated tickets, so they are shown as related context, not as close matches.
useful_semantic_alone_min is set above the highest semantic cosine seen for a query with no useful past ticket (0.82).
calibration.limits: Cut points were chosen on 28 queries against 40 tickets. Several margins are 0.03 to 0.04 wide. They must be re-tuned whenever the tickets, the model or the keyword settings change.
